cards.title: The same few parts
cards.body:
Phones, laptops, tablets and games consoles look very different on the outside. Inside, they're surprisingly alike: nearly all of them are built from the **same handful of parts**.

In this lesson you'll open up a laptop and a phone, find those parts, and learn what each one does.

cards.title: Before we open anything
cards.body:
Everything you take apart in this course is a **simulation**: tap and drag as much as you like.

Real phones and laptops are different. **Don't open one without an adult or a repair shop.** It can break parts, it can end the device's warranty (the maker's promise to fix it for free), and the **lithium battery inside can catch fire if it's bent or punctured**.

cards.prompt: Here's the inside of a laptop, with its bottom panel off. **Tap each part** to find out what it is and what it does.

parts.job: The big board everything plugs into. Its thin lines carry signals between the parts, like roads.
The brain (central processing unit). It follows the instructions that make apps work.
Blows hot air out through the vents, so the CPU doesn't overheat.
RAM (random-access memory): a fast workspace for whatever you're using right now.
Keeps your photos, apps and files, even when the power is off.
Stores the energy that runs everything. It's the biggest part inside.
Joins the battery to the board. Technicians unplug it first, so nothing gets power.

cards.explanation: Almost every laptop has these same parts. Look for the clues: the fan's blades, the RAM's row of chips, the storage chip's stacked layers and the battery's lightning bolt.

cards.prompt: Now open a laptop yourself. Take out the **four screws**, lift off the **bottom panel**, then **unplug the battery** before touching anything else.

actions.nudge: Unscrew this one first.
Unscrew this one first.
Unscrew this one first.
Unscrew this one first.
The panel won't lift until all four screws are out.
Lift the panel off first.

cards.explanation: Screws first, then the panel. Then technicians **unplug the battery** before they touch any other part, so nothing gets a jolt of power while they work.

cards.prompt: Here's the inside. Label the five main parts.
cards.explanation: The **battery** is the biggest part. The square chip is the **CPU**, cooled by the round **fan** next to it. The long stick with little chips is **RAM**, and the smaller card is **storage**.

cards.prompt: Match each part to its job.
cards.explanation: The **CPU** does the work, **RAM** holds what's in use, **storage** keeps things for later, the **motherboard** links everything, and the **battery** powers it all.

cards.prompt: A phone has the same jobs to do, squeezed into a much smaller space. **Tap each part** to meet it.

parts.job: The phone's motherboard. The main chips are packed onto this one small board.
Takes your photos and videos, through a lens in the back cover.
The same job as in a laptop: it follows the instructions, on a smaller chip.
A fast workspace for the apps open right now. It's cleared when the phone turns off.
Keeps your photos, apps and messages, even when the phone is off.
Stores the energy. It fills most of the phone, so it can last all day.
Joins the battery to the board. It's unplugged first in every repair.
Where the charger plugs in. It's on the outside edge, so pocket fluff can get in.

cards.explanation: Same parts, same looks as the laptop, just smaller: the CPU's shiny lid, RAM's row of chips and storage's stacked layers. Most phones have no fan.

cards.prompt: Now a phone. It's a tighter squeeze, but the same parts are inside. Open it up and unplug its battery.

actions.nudge: Unscrew this one first.
Unscrew this one first.
Both screws have to come out first.
Take the back cover off first.

cards.explanation: Same pattern as the laptop: screws, cover, then **unplug the battery** first, the way technicians keep themselves and the phone safe. Real phones are also sealed with strong glue, which repair shops soften with gentle heat.

cards.prompt: Tap the part where this phone keeps your **photos**, even when it's switched off.
cards.explanation: Photos live in **storage**, which keeps everything when the power is off. RAM only holds what's in use right now, and forgets it all when the phone turns off.

cards.prompt: Label the phone's parts. They're smaller and packed tighter than the laptop's.
cards.explanation: A phone squeezes the **CPU**, **RAM** and **storage** onto one small board at the top, with the **camera** beside them. The **battery** takes up most of the space, because it has to last all day.

cards.prompt: A repair: swap this phone's camera, then put the phone back together in a safe order.

actions.nudge: Unscrew this one first.
Unscrew this one first.
Both screws have to come out first.
Take the back cover off first.
Unplug the battery before touching any other part.
Take the old camera out first.
Fit the new camera before reconnecting the battery.
Reconnect the battery before closing it up.
Put the back cover on first.
Put the back cover on first.

cards.explanation: Putting a device back together is taking it apart in reverse. The battery is **unplugged first** and **plugged back in last**, just before the cover goes on, so no part is ever worked on with power connected.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Phones and laptops are built from the same parts: **CPU**, **RAM**, **storage**, a **battery**, and the **motherboard** that connects them.
- The CPU does the work, RAM holds what's in use now, and storage keeps things for later.
- Technicians **unplug the battery first** and plug it back in last.
- Real devices should only be opened by an adult or a repair shop.

Next: why RAM and storage are so different.
